pr_title: Enable size-optimized LINQ build for Browser
pr_body:
Re-enable the size-optimized variant of LINQ and use it for the Browser build of the library. (This was previously added not for IL size but for AOT asm size, but it's also just less IL.)

This reduces the size of a default Blazor wasm app by ~20K uncompressed and ~7K compressed.

Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/45399
cc: @eerhardt, @tannergooding

issue_context.title: Consider using .SizeOpt.cs in System.Linq built for Browser/Xamarin/AOT
issue_context.body:
We previously added the *.SizeOpt.cs set of implementations for System.Linq.dll in order to cull out some generics-heavy optimizations that were adding significant overhead (often megabytes of asm in an app) to AOT compilations using LINQ.  However, it also adds non-trivial IL size, e.g. a .dll built with the SpeedOpt files is currently ~128K whereas one built with the SizeOpt files is currently ~102K (both sizes are untrimmed).

For target frameworks where size is at a premium, we should consider using these .SizeOpt variants instead.

For AOT builds, we should also look to use these SizeOpt variants.

And if we're not going to use them in either, we should delete them and clean up the cruft. (We also should revisit a few specific optimizations, in particular the ToArray implementation that uses a complicated and large "LargeArrayBuilder", which is likely not worth its weight.)

cc: @marek-safar, @eerhardt

review_comments:
Is this behavior still something we can preserve even if `IsSizeOptimized`?

If not, it would be nice to add comments on why these tests are skipped. Reading the comment below makes it sound like these tests should work on all .NET Core builds.

> Is this behavior still something we can preserve even if IsSizeOptimized?

Not without adding more code back to the size-optimized implementation. The comment below assumes the optimizations in the .Speed.cs implementation, which recognizes "partitions" and thus know that Skip(2) on an empty partition is also empty.  The Size implementation loses all such optimizations.
